items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: one time I even got on a thing where I used to use the pedal a lot and try to play like Lionel Hampton

ctx.x: Yes, it was. O'Neil Spencer, a very popular drummer then. But that was the tightest little band that I ever heard, and they made a specialty of playing some of the classics, things like some of Chopin's pieces, Edward Grieg, and these things that were arranged... I understand Charlie Shavers did most of the arranging. And they were really arranged in a very unique way. They also had a thing they used to play called "From A-Flat to C," which turned out to be a set of changes that a lot of musicians use now, which…

Billy Kyle had a style that I always felt like was like somewhere between Teddy Wilson and Earl Hines. He had the fast fingers like Teddy Wilson had, but he also had the punch of Earl Hines. With these different pianists, I would hear one, and for the next month or six weeks, I would be trying to play like him, and then next time you'd hear me, I'd be playing like somebody else. As a matter of fact, one time I even got on a thing where I used to use the pedal a lot and try to play like Lionel Hampton -- not like…

piano, but to try to make the piano sound like a vibraharp! Which didn't turn out to be very successful. But a young guy learning like that, you begin to be... You are inspired by so many different people, you know. I guess in trying to grab a little of all of these people, you eventually come into your own with something.
